title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard processes for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and commonly used internal templates. It provides a single reference for owners, requesters, approvers, and auditors.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors.
- Covers systems and processes owned by Product, Engineering, Security, People Ops, Finance, and Legal.
- Excludes lab notebooks and personal devices not used for company work (see device policy for exceptions).

Owner & escalation:
- Primary owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood.example.com).
- Security review owner: Security & Compliance (security@redwood.example.com).
- Procurement & contracts: Finance & Legal (procurement@redwood.example.com).
- For urgent incidents or access escalations outside business hours: Pager duty for Security (see oncall page).

1) Access & Permissions
Principles:
- Principle of least privilege: grant the minimum access required for job function.
- Role-based access: prefer scoped groups/roles over individual grants.
- Time-bound access: elevated access should have expiry.
- Auditability: all grants must be request-tracked with an approver.

Standard request flow (non-production):
1. Requester files an Access Request via the internal Access Request form (Confluence link / request portal).
2. Team Lead approves access for team-level resources.
3. System owner grants access and records the grant in the request ticket.
4. Access is auto-expired if flagged as temporary; otherwise reviewed quarterly.

Production and sensitive data access (must include justification):
- Approval matrix (summary):
| Request type | Required approver(s) | SLA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Team access (non-prod) | Team Lead | 3 business days |
| Production read-only | Engineering Manager + Security | 2 business days |
| Production write / deploy | Engineering Manager + Security + Release Manager | 1 business day |
| Sensitive data export | VP Eng + Security + Legal | 5 business days |

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Use the break-glass workflow in the request portal. Break-glass requires after-the-fact review within 24 hours by Security and the owner_team. All sessions captured and recorded.

SSO / Directory rules:
- Redwood uses Okta as primary IdP. Group naming convention: rw-<team>-<role> (e.g., rw-platform-admins).
- Service accounts must be approved by Security and owned by a named on-call rotation.

2) Change Management
When to use change process:
- Any change to production services, infra (network, IAM, firewall), external-facing APIs, or database schema requires a change request.
- Low-risk operational changes (routine patching, scheduled cron updates) may follow the standard operational change template.

Standard change model:
- Submit Change Request using the Change Request template (see Templates section).
- Required fields: description, scope, impact, rollback plan, blast radius, owners, scheduled window, validation plan.
- Changes classified as: Standard (pre-approved), Normal (CAB approval), Emergency (post-facto CAB review).

Change approval and CAB:
- Normal changes reviewed by weekly CAB (Change Advisory Board): Engineering, Platform, SRE, Security, Product, and an on-call representative.
- Approval criteria: risk acceptable, rollback plan validated, monitoring in place.

Change request template (sample):
| Field | Example/Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Title | deploy: v1.4.2 runtime patch |
| Owner | Marina Lopez (marina@redwood.example.com) |
| Window | 2026-12-10 02:00-03:00 UTC |
| Risk | moderate (single region downtime possible) |
| Rollback | run rollback script: ./scripts/rollback-1.4.2.sh |
| Validation | smoke tests: /tests/smoke/run.sh, latency check < 200ms |

Emergency change procedure:
1. Execute emergency change if needed to restore service.
2. Notify oncall and open an incident.
3. Create a change record within 4 hours for CAB post-facto review.

3) Data Management
Data classification:
- Public: information intended for public consumption.
- Internal: company-internal, not for public release.
- Confidential: customer data, financials, PII, sensitive contracts.

Retention & storage (high level):
| Data type | Storage location | Retention period | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Logging (non-sensitive) | Centralized ELK | 90 days | Eng-Platform |
| Audit logs | Immutable S3 (encrypted) | 7 years | Security |
| Customer PII | Encrypted DB (region-specific) | As per contract | Product/Legal |
| Backups (db) | Encrypted, geo-redundant | 30 days | Eng-Infra |

Data export & sharing:
- Export of Confidential data requires signed approval from Product, Security, and Legal.
- All exports must be tracked via the Data Export form and recorded in the export ledger.

Encryption & key management:
- All confidential data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Use customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments. Key rotation policy: annual rotation for master keys, monthly for data-encryption keys.

Privacy & compliance:
- Follow the Data Processing Addendum (DPA) for customer data. See compliance-evidence page for controls mapping.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Procurement thresholds and approvals:
| Amount (USD) | Required approver(s) |
| --- | --- |
| <$1,000 | Requester manager |
| $1,000 - $25,000 | Department head + Finance reviewer |
| >$25,000 | VP + Finance + Legal (if contract) |

Vendor onboarding checklist (procurement stage):
- Business justification and ROI estimate.
- Security questionnaire completed and reviewed by Security.
- Contract template reviewed by Legal.
- PO created and Finance approves.

Expenses & travel reimbursement:
- Employees should use the corporate travel portal for bookings. When unavailable, reimbursement requires receipts and an expense report within 30 days.
- Per diem: $75 domestic / $120 international (standard); see Finance for country-specific rates.
- Non-compliant expenses (alcohol except client entertainment pre-approved) are not reimbursed.

5) Vendor Management
Roles & responsibilities:
- Vendor owner (business sponsor): owns relationship and ROI tracking.
- Security: performs risk assessment and ongoing security posture reviews.
- Procurement/Legal: negotiates terms and maintains signed contracts.

Ongoing vendor reviews:
- Annual security review for vendors with access to sensitive systems or data.
- Quarterly business reviews for strategic vendors (> $50k annual spend).

Termination/ offboarding:
- Revoke all access, collect credentials, confirm data deletion or return per contract, and maintain an offboarding report in the vendor file.

6) Travel policies
Booking and approvals:
- Domestic economy coach class for <6 hour flights; premium economy or business requires VP approval.
- Hotel stays should be standard business class; upgrades require justification.
- Conference travel requires manager pre-approval and a short post-travel summary.

Advance notice & emergency changes:
- Request travel at least 14 days in advance for international travel, 7 days for domestic.
- Emergency trips may be booked with manager approval and must be documented in an expense report.

COVID / health & safety (where applicable):
- Follow local health guidance; People Ops maintains a page with international travel advisories and insurance information.

7) Internal templates (quick links and snippets)
Access Request template (fields):
- Requester name; team; resource(s); access level; justification; duration; approver(s).

Change Request (fields):
- Title; owner; scheduled window; impact; rollback; monitoring steps; CAB decision.

Vendor evaluation (short form):
- Vendor name; product summary; security score (0-100); legal issues; TCO estimate; recommended action.

Expense report template (fields):
- Employee; date; expense type; amount; currency; receipt attached (Y/N); project code; manager approval.

Appendix: SLAs & operational thresholds
- Access request SLA: standard 3 business days; expedited 1 business day; break-glass immediate.
- Change approval target: Normal change review within 5 business days of submission.
- Vendor security review: 10 business days target for initial assessment.

Related resources and links:
- Access request portal: /internal/access-requests
- Change request template: /internal/change-requests/templates
- Data export form: /security/data-exports
- Procurement portal: /finance/procurement
- Vendor registry: /finance/vendors

Contact list:
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.example.com
- Security: security@redwood.example.com
- Procurement & Finance: procurement@redwood.example.com

Revision history:

End of document.
